data.name: AffordaGolf Online
data.detailed_description:
Características

  • Online Multiplayer up to 127 players in same map on Player hosted rooms. (Server Browser)
  • Online Multiplayer up to 12 players in same map on Steam hosted Lobbies. (Matchmaking)
  • Ball Customization, any texture and color of your desire can be added to your ball.
  • Trail Customization, any texture and color of your desire can be added to your trail.
  • Map Editor, create, edit and publish your own maps and let everyone play in them.
  • 9 Default maps
  • User created maps
  • Steam Cards
  • Steam Achievements
  • Steam Leaderboards
  • Steam Workshop
  • No EARLY ACCESS


Acerca do jogo

AffordaGolf is a Multiplayer Online Mini-golf game!

In AffordaGolf you can play mini-golf with your friends and up to 127 people on unlimited amount of maps (courses).

Features

  • Online Multiplayer up to 127 players in same map on Player hosted rooms. (Server Browser)
  • Online Multiplayer up to 12 players in same map on Steam hosted Lobbies. (Matchmaking)

  • Ball Customization, any texture and color of your desire can be added to your ball.

  • Trail Customization, any texture and color of your desire can be added to your trail.

  • Map Editor, create, edit and publish your own maps and let everyone play in them.

  • 9 Default Maps
  • User created maps.

  • Steam Cards
  • Steam Achievements
  • Steam Stats and Cloud
  • Steam Workshop
  • No EARLY ACCESS

In AffordaGolf you can play with your friends like you want, affordable!

reviews.review:
AffordaGolf Online is a lightweight multiplayer miniature-golf game developed and published by Oryzhon Studios. Released on Steam in December 2016, it takes the familiar idea of mini-golf and builds a social online experience around it. Instead of attempting to reproduce realistic professional golf, the game concentrates on accessible controls, unusual courses, multiplayer competition, customization, and community-created content. Its straightforward concept makes it easy to understand, while the multiplayer and creation systems provide most of the depth available beyond simply getting the ball into each hole.

One of the game's defining characteristics is the size of its multiplayer sessions. Player-hosted rooms can accommodate as many as 127 participants on a map, while Steam-hosted matchmaking supports smaller groups of up to 12 players. This gives AffordaGolf Online an unusually ambitious multiplayer structure for such a simple game. Traditional sessions with a handful of friends can feel like ordinary competitive mini-golf, whereas heavily populated rooms can become chaotic events where the social spectacle is almost as important as achieving a good score. The basic challenge still revolves around judging shot direction and strength while dealing with obstacles and the shape of each course.

AffordaGolf Online includes nine standard maps, but its built-in map editor is considerably more important to its long-term variety. Players can construct their own courses and share them with the community through Steam Workshop support. This is an excellent match for miniature golf because handcrafted obstacles and unconventional layouts are naturally suited to experimentation. Once the official courses become familiar, community creations can introduce new challenges without requiring additional official content. The downside is that user-created maps can vary considerably in quality, balance, difficulty, and visual presentation, so the experience will not always be consistent.

Customization is another major part of the game's identity. Players can alter their golf balls with different colors and textures and can also personalize the trails that follow them. The ability to use custom images gives players substantially more freedom than a fixed selection of cosmetic unlocks would provide. It works particularly well when playing privately with friends, where everyone can create a recognizable appearance. However, the freedom to use custom imagery also means that public multiplayer sessions can potentially expose players to material uploaded by strangers. The developer makes clear that responsibility for those images belongs to the individual users and explains how the game handles them.

The Steam integration is fairly extensive for a modest indie release. AffordaGolf Online features achievements, statistics, leaderboards, Steam Cloud functionality, Trading Cards, Workshop support, online competitive and cooperative functionality, and its level editor. These additions help give players objectives outside individual matches. Leaderboards can encourage players to improve their performance, while achievements provide additional goals for completion-oriented users. Workshop integration remains the standout feature because it directly expands the playable content and gives creative players a reason to remain involved after learning the official courses.

Presentation is considerably more functional than spectacular. AffordaGolf Online was designed to run on modest computers, and its original hardware requirements were extremely accessible even by the standards of its release period. That accessibility benefits a multiplayer game because friends do not need powerful gaming systems merely to participate. At the same time, players accustomed to more polished modern sports and party games should temper their expectations. The visuals are basic, and the overall production reflects the game's small-scale indie origins rather than attempting elaborate environments, realistic golf physics, or cinematic presentation.

Its greatest weakness today comes from the same area that once represented its greatest strength: multiplayer. A game built around online interaction becomes significantly dependent on the availability of other players. The large theoretical player capacity sounds impressive, but it matters much less when there are not enough active participants to fill public matches. AffordaGolf Online therefore makes more sense for players who can bring friends with them than for someone expecting a consistently populated competitive community. With a prepared group, the maps, custom courses, personalized balls, and unpredictable multiplayer situations can still provide entertaining sessions.

There is also relatively little here for players seeking a substantial solo progression system or a detailed simulation of golf. AffordaGolf Online is fundamentally a casual social game, and its simplicity is intentional. Players who enjoy experimenting with physics, trying strange Workshop maps, creating courses, and competing informally are likely to appreciate it more than those looking for sophisticated sports mechanics. The game is at its best when treated as a sandbox-like party activity rather than a serious test of golfing realism.

Overall, AffordaGolf Online is an interesting example of a small indie game attempting to extend a simple concept through multiplayer scale and community creativity. Oryzhon Studios supplied a functional miniature-golf foundation and supplemented it with large player-hosted rooms, matchmaking, customization, a course editor, Workshop sharing, achievements, statistics, and leaderboards. Its dated presentation, reliance on an active multiplayer environment, and uneven user-generated content prevent it from feeling like a particularly polished package today, but its free-to-play structure makes experimentation relatively easy. For a group of friends willing to create or download courses and embrace the game's casual chaos, there is still some enjoyable miniature-golf entertainment to be found.

Rating: 5/10
